findings.reason: a prior-art pass at each base revision would have shrunk §7/§9/§11 from "add the check" to "measure what already holds and guard the one gap", which is exactly what the shipped nodes ended up doing after the fact.
findings.text: §9's done-when named `set section_declarations.<id>`, which already moved the typed record at its base (the plan's own landed comment `c-pwnf-s9-landed` records that the dotted form was the test's positive control and the refusal came only from the whole-map form); §11's recorded escape likewise did not reproduce at main (`c-pwnf-s11-landed`: "every op path of `_edit_plan` already returns the identical structured version-conflict refusal"), and §7's "consider having the guard mint the id" proposes machinery `_gen_id` already provides on every append path. Each section proposed a mechanism whose owner already existed, so the guard work must be scoped to the real delta — the whole-map declaration write (§9) and the pre-existing uniform refusal (§11) — not to a mechanism being rebuilt

findings.reason: naming `_refuse_duplicate_id` as the single owner and having the north-star and sprint paths call it is a smaller, more honest change than shipping a third detector, and is the extension the plan's own §7 evidence pointed at.
findings.text: §7 adds `_refuse_duplicate_id` as the owner of "refuse an append whose id already addresses an entry", and applies it across sections/followups/research/questions/comments/decisions, but two other collections still enforce the same rule with their own code: `_check_north_star_ids` (`reckon/_store.py:2262`, raising `duplicate north-star id`) and `_create_sprint` (`reckon/mcp.py:2891`, `sprint ... already exists`). The design cites the sprint check as prior art (plan §7, "sprint add refuses duplicates (`mcp.py:2908`)") and then leaves it beside the new helper instead of routing it through it, so the uniqueness rule now has three owners and drifts

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the result the plan exists to produce (version check, per-file lock and commutative comment merge as one step) hides behind the store's existing `write_plan` / `_write_state` entry point; the plan adds no parallel module surface, and §6–§12 land tests and one shared helper rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 ships `_refuse_duplicate_id` (`reckon/_store.py:2342`) as a third independent duplicate-id detector beside `_check_north_star_ids` and `_create_sprint`, rather than extending the rule's existing owners.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §9 and §11 each propose a guard (or a done-when) for behaviour that already existed at the section's own base revision, so the plan did not search the owner before proposing the mechanism.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §7's duplicate-id refusal and §10's ordered-replacement batch add behaviour (a refusal, a one-version batch) rather than forwarding to an existing reader, and the collision payload (§7 `existing_item`) is a structured field the writer acts on, not a restatement of the message.
